A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ranking study with the same authors, algorithms, and datasets. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, allowing equations, experiments, tables, and figures to be matched across relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original transitivity, prediction accuracy, ranking correlation, and hyperparameter sensitivity analyses on Chatbot Arena and SLAM, including per-model results and permutation experiments in the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds two 10,000-permutation Elo evaluations and statistical analyses of cyclic preferences in both datasets.

M1.justification: The Elo, Bradley-Terry, Glicko, and Markov ranking procedures remain unchanged. Glicko and Markov equations move to Appendices A.1–A.2. The new consistency analysis evaluates the data without modifying the ranking algorithms.

E1.justification: Both versions use Chatbot Arena with 57 models and 244,978 matchups, and SLAM with 11 models and 2,858 matchups. The added permutation and consistency analyses reuse these datasets without introducing new task requirements or populations.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison methods remain Elo, Markov, Glicko, and Bradley-Terry, with win rate retained in Table 3's correlation comparison. The weighted-logistic discussion also appears in both versions.

E3.justification: Appendix A.5 adds an Elo setting with K = 25 and 10,000 permutations per evaluation; A.6 introduces a cycle-based dataset consistency test. The original 75/25 split, F1 evaluation, 100-value hyperparameter sweeps, and K = 3/5 permutation experiments remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a targeted check of whether Elo rankings stabilize at 10,000 permutations (A.5, Figure 6) and an analysis of whether cyclic preferences indicate inconsistent human judgments (A.6, Table 5). Existing sensitivity analyses and model-specific error examples are retained.

E5.justification: v2 adds chi-squared significance tests and p-values for dataset consistency, explicitly describes two separate evaluations in A.5, and reports a bootstrap confidence interval attributed to Chatbot Arena in Section 4.3. These additions do not establish additional repetitions of the original benchmark experiments.

E6.justification: Table 2 reverses the Arena/SLAM F1 assignments, correcting their disagreement with the existing discussion and unchanged Figures 3–4: for example, Elo's Arena/SLAM values change from 0.87/0.90 to 0.90/0.87. Figure 6 adds rank-reversal results, and Table 5 reports 19 SLAM and 393 Arena cycles, with chi-squared values 45.06 and 1107.25.

T1.justification: Appendix A.6 adds a formal cycle definition, an adjacency-matrix formula for counting three-model cycles, and chi-squared and degrees-of-freedom formulas. v1's explicit Bradley-Terry logistic and log-likelihood expressions are omitted. The transitivity definition and relocated Glicko/Markov equations remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a systematic comparison of ranking algorithms using transitivity, prediction accuracy, and stability, leading to dataset-dependent selection guidelines. v2 foregrounds Elo's instability in the introduction, but this finding and the recommendation against Elo already appear in v1.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 newly distinguishes transitive ranking outputs from preservation of transitive relationships in human data. Section 4.3 explains that a narrow bootstrap interval need not imply prediction accuracy against unseen opponents. A.6 newly interprets cycle-test results as supporting judgment quality; the original limitations and principal recommendations remain.

D1.justification: v1 supplies an explicit code-repository link in the introduction's footnote. v2 removes that link while retaining the statement that code, data, and models are released. The relocated Glicko and Markov equations do not constitute newly disclosed implementations.

R1.justification: v2 adds Guo et al. and Dubois et al. in the introduction and Kendall and Smith and Sanjaya et al. for the consistency analysis, while removing Jiang et al. It more explicitly contrasts its scope with Boubdir et al.'s Elo-focused study, retaining the original overall novelty claim.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around explicit research-gap and contribution bullets. v2 shortens background, sensitivity, and related-work prose, moves algorithm equations into the appendix, converts several numbered subsections into paragraph headings, and reframes Discussion as Recommended Best Practices.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 6, Table 5, emphasized findings, and four shaded best-practice boxes. Existing figures and tables are resized or relocated, including regrouping the appendix F1 plots. Figures 2–5 retain their plotted content; several captions are revised.

improvement.justification: Correcting Table 2 resolves a concrete contradiction with the dataset-specific discussion and appendix plots. Clearer organization and transitivity explanations, together with additional Elo stability evidence, provide limited quality gains. These benefits are tempered by removal of the code-access link and incomplete specification of the new consistency test, including an unexplained d in Equation 11; its conclusions about judge quality therefore warrant caution.
